83	## 5. Decisions
84	
85	### Decision D1
86	- Basis: R6, R8
87	- Minimal option: manter um comando por vez e medir
88	- Selected option: duas faixas com slots e fila limitada, por comando conhecido (curto ou pesado)
89	- Rationale: a consulta curta de 10 ms não deve esperar o check de 25 s; os comandos são seguros em paralelo como o são em processos separados (as escritas de derivados são atômicas, spec `pose-writer-coordination-and-atomic-publication`); a classificação é uma lista declarada e medida, não uma heurística
90	- Consequences: um comando novo é pesado até ser medido e listado; os padrões (1 pesado, 2 curtos) foram escolhidos para a máquina medida e são configuráveis
91	- Falsifier: uma consulta curta que espera um check pesado, ou uma fila que cresce além do limite
92	
93	## 6. Validation
94	
95	### Strategy
96	
97	Testes com um comando lento injetado provam o isolamento das faixas, a recusa por fila cheia e as métricas; a medição no repositório real é o teste opt-in, rodada uma vez com o resultado no relatório.
98	
99	### Deterministic checks
100	
101	`go test -race` dos testes do rastreio; a matriz estrita em clone limpo; a medição opt-in registrada em `.pose/reports/`.
102

104	- R6 [satisfied] test:TestAShortQueryIsNotQueuedBehindAHeavyCheckAndAFullLaneRefuses check:runtime-qos-integration
105	- R8 [satisfied] test:TestMeasureTheRuntimeOnTheRealRepository
106	
107	### Known gaps
108	- A medição é de um ambiente (declarado no relatório) e de um repositório; não vale para outros tamanhos de histórico.
109	- Dois comandos que chegam no mesmo instante ao último slot livre podem ambos esperar: a fila pode passar do limite pelos chegados daquele instante.

**decision: changes-requested**

The lanes themselves work. The problem is that the per-lane metrics R6 requires never reach the operator: `pose runtime status` (JSON or text) doesn't print them. The one measurement run shows this: it recorded `runtime_metrics: null`, and its report has `?` placeholders for those counts. The docs promise those fields in `status`. That's a medium-severity defect, and the policy only accepts low-severity risks, so I can't approve.

I had no shell access (the Bash tool was denied), so I didn't run any tests or tools myself. This review relies on reading the code at `95af7b63` and the sealed evidence.

## What I checked in the code

- **Lanes:** `runtime_lanes.go` keeps its counts consistently. A command is counted when it enters a lane, and on every exit path the count is released, including deadline and shutdown withdrawals (`runtime_host.go:106-127`). `surface-check` goes to the short lane and everything else to the heavy lane, which matches the timings in the spec (about 10 ms against 25 s and 160 s).
- **Flags:** the numeric flags are bounded and their error messages are clear (`runtime_cmd.go:118-142`). `start` passes them on to the detached `serve` (`runtime_cmd.go:105-108`, `195`).
- **Thresholds:** T1 0.60, T2 0.80, T3 3× or 250 ms, T4 1536 MiB and T6 500 ms are the same in the test (`runtime_measure_test.go:32-37`), in spec R8 and in the report. The report's `repo_head` is `7c2abbf6`, the commit that added the test and its thresholds. Without git I couldn't confirm that the spec text already had them before that run.
- **Running commands in parallel in one process:** this is now possible, and the D1 rationale only argues from separate processes. On the plus side, the resident memo is protected by a lock (`resident_git_memo.go:20`) and no hosted path changes the working directory or environment. But the `-race` test only runs `surface-check --help` alongside a heavy check, so the real `surface-check` code path was never race-checked in the same process.

## Findings

| id | sev | where | summary |
|---|---|---|---|

**decision: changes-requested**

The lanes themselves work. The problem is that the per-lane metrics R6 requires never reach the operator: `pose runtime status` (JSON or text) doesn't print them. The one measurement run shows this: it recorded `runtime_metrics: null`, and its report has `?` placeholders for those counts. The docs promise those fields in `status`. That's a medium-severity defect, and the policy only accepts low-severity risks, so I can't approve.

I had no shell access (the Bash tool was denied), so I didn't run any tests or tools myself. This review relies on reading the code at `95af7b63` and the sealed evidence.

## What I checked in the code

- **Lanes:** `runtime_lanes.go` keeps its counts consistently. A command is counted when it enters a lane, and on every exit path the count is released, including deadline and shutdown withdrawals (`runtime_host.go:106-127`). `surface-check` goes to the short lane and everything else to the heavy lane, which matches the timings in the spec (about 10 ms against 25 s and 160 s).
- **Flags:** the numeric flags are bounded and their error messages are clear (`runtime_cmd.go:118-142`). `start` passes them on to the detached `serve` (`runtime_cmd.go:105-108`, `195`).
- **Thresholds:** T1 0.60, T2 0.80, T3 3× or 250 ms, T4 1536 MiB and T6 500 ms are the same in the test (`runtime_measure_test.go:32-37`), in spec R8 and in the report. The report's `repo_head` is `7c2abbf6`, the commit that added the test and its thresholds. Without git I couldn't confirm that the spec text already had them before that run.
- **Running commands in parallel in one process:** this is now possible, and the D1 rationale only argues from separate processes. On the plus side, the resident memo is protected by a lock (`resident_git_memo.go:20`) and no hosted path changes the working directory or environment. But the `-race` test only runs `surface-check --help` alongside a heavy check, so the real `surface-check` code path was never race-checked in the same process.
